abstract: Maintains protocol validation filings, microstructural resolution benchmarks, and destructive micro-sampling duration records
system_message:
You are Metallurgical Forensics Lead (MET). The Metallurgical Forensics Lead (MET) tracks forensic qualification dossiers, instrument spatial resolution benchmarks, destructive specimen preparation requirements, and Vickers microhardness profiling for investigative methods considered in turbine rotor failure evaluations.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Vickers Microhardness Profiling（HARD）
information_points.content:
MET-HARD-JRM：Under the Vickers Microhardness Profiling assessment, the Resonant Ultrasonic Spectroscopy Protocol demonstrates an average matrix microhardness of 310 HV across ten coupon indentations.
MET-HARD-UCV：Under the Vickers Microhardness Profiling assessment, the Synchrotron Micro-X-Ray Diffraction Protocol is associated with an average matrix microhardness of 380 HV across the heat-affected zone specimen coupons.
MET-HARD-54K：Under the Vickers Microhardness Profiling assessment, survey logs for the Focused Ion Beam Electron Backscatter Protocol establish an average matrix microhardness of 345 HV within the heat-affected zone specimen coupons.

information_points.title: Maintains protocol validation filings, microstructural resolution benchmarks, and destructive micro-sampling duration records（MICRO）
information_points.content:
MET-MICRO-0IA：For the Synchrotron Micro-X-Ray Diffraction Protocol, validated protocol documentation filed is recorded as true with formal qualification sign-off by the accredited metallurgical oversight board. The procedure exhibits a microstructural resolution limit of 35 nm for target fracture surface imaging, and requires a destructive micro-sampling duration of 30 h to excise and prepare micro-samples from fractured blade roots.
MET-MICRO-FI2：Regarding the Resonant Ultrasonic Spectroscopy Protocol, validated protocol documentation filed is confirmed as true per the forensic qualification dossier. Its microstructural resolution limit is 65 nm under incident beam conditions, and the protocol involves a destructive micro-sampling duration of 30 h for hot cell coupon extraction and preparation.
MET-MICRO-4HM：Records for the Focused Ion Beam Electron Backscatter Protocol indicate that validated protocol documentation filed is true based on oversight board approval. Its microstructural resolution limit stands at 35 nm for grain boundary imaging, accompanied by a destructive micro-sampling duration of 30 h to complete coupon lift-out and electro-polishing.
